_meta.about: Curated World Explorer content. 'wiki' is the English Wikipedia article used at build time (scripts/build-media.mjs) to fetch the photo, its Wikimedia Commons credit and licence, and map coordinates. Coordinates and images are never typed by hand.

landmarks.name: Taj Mahal
landmarks.why: A white marble tomb built by emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
facts: Its marble seems to change colour — pinkish at dawn, white at noon and golden in the evening light.
It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

landmarks.name: Red Fort
landmarks.why: The red sandstone palace-fort of the Mughal emperors in Delhi.
facts: Every Independence Day, the Prime Minister raises India's flag here.
It is named after its huge red sandstone walls.

landmarks.name: India Gate
landmarks.why: A war memorial for Indian soldiers who died in the First World War.
facts: The names of thousands of soldiers are carved on its walls.
It stands at one end of Kartavya Path, where the Republic Day parade takes place.

landmarks.name: Hampi
landmarks.why: The ruins of Vijayanagara, once one of the richest cities in the world.
facts: Its stone chariot at the Vittala Temple is pictured on India's ₹50 note.
Giant boulders lie everywhere around the ruins.

landmarks.name: Gateway of India
landmarks.why: A grand arch by the sea, built to welcome visitors arriving in Mumbai by ship.
facts: It faces the Arabian Sea.
Boats leave from here for Elephanta Island and its cave temples.

landmarks.name: Brihadeeswarar Temple
landmarks.why: A huge granite temple built by the Chola king Rajaraja I, over 1,000 years old.
facts: Its tower, the vimana, is about 66 metres tall.
It is part of the UNESCO site 'Great Living Chola Temples'.

landmarks.name: Eiffel Tower
landmarks.why: Built for the 1889 World's Fair, it became the symbol of Paris.
facts: It is painted every few years to protect the iron from rust.
It was the tallest structure in the world until 1930.

landmarks.name: Louvre Museum
landmarks.style: French Renaissance palace with a modern glass pyramid
landmarks.why: The world's most-visited art museum, home of the Mona Lisa.
facts: It was once a royal palace.
The glass pyramid at its entrance opened in 1989.

landmarks.name: Palace of Versailles
landmarks.why: The giant palace of King Louis XIV, famous for its Hall of Mirrors.
facts: The Hall of Mirrors has 357 mirrors.
Its gardens have hundreds of fountains and statues.

landmarks.name: Great Pyramid of Giza
landmarks.why: The oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World — and the only one still standing.
facts: It was built as a tomb for the pharaoh Khufu.
For nearly 4,000 years it was the tallest building made by people.

landmarks.name: Great Sphinx of Giza
landmarks.why: A giant statue with a lion's body and a human head, carved from rock.
facts: It is carved out of one single piece of limestone bedrock.
Its nose has been missing for hundreds of years.

landmarks.name: Colosseum
landmarks.why: The largest amphitheatre ever built in ancient Rome.
facts: It could hold around 50,000 people.
Part of its floor had hidden tunnels and lifts for animals.

landmarks.name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
landmarks.why: A bell tower that started leaning because the ground under it is soft.
facts: It began to lean while it was still being built.
Engineers have made it lean a little less so it stays safe.

landmarks.name: Statue of Liberty
landmarks.why: A gift from France to the United States, a symbol of freedom.
facts: It is made of copper and turned green over time.
Her torch is held up about 93 metres above the ground (including the pedestal).

landmarks.name: Grand Canyon
landmarks.why: A gigantic canyon carved by the Colorado River.
facts: In places it is more than 1.6 kilometres deep.
Its rock layers show nearly 2 billion years of Earth's history.

landmarks.name: Great Wall of China
landmarks.period: Built over many centuries; most of today's wall is from the Ming dynasty
landmarks.why: A series of walls built to protect China's northern borders.
facts: All its sections together stretch for thousands of kilometres.
Watchtowers along the wall used smoke signals to send messages.

landmarks.name: Machu Picchu
landmarks.why: A stone city of the Inca high up in the Andes mountains.
facts: Its stones fit so tightly that no mortar was used.
It stands on a mountain ridge about 2,400 metres above sea level.

landmarks.name: Christ the Redeemer
landmarks.why: A giant statue with open arms on top of Corcovado mountain.
facts: Its arms stretch about 28 metres from hand to hand.
It is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

landmarks.name: Sydney Opera House
landmarks.why: Famous for its roof that looks like sails or shells.
facts: Its roof is covered with more than a million tiles.
It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

landmarks.name: Big Ben
landmarks.why: The great bell in the clock tower of the Houses of Parliament.
facts: 'Big Ben' is really the name of the bell; the tower is the Elizabeth Tower.
Its clock faces are about 7 metres across.

landmarks.name: Angkor Wat
landmarks.why: The largest religious monument in the world.
facts: It appears on Cambodia's national flag.
It was first built as a Hindu temple for the god Vishnu.

landmarks.name: Petra
landmarks.why: A city carved straight into rose-pink cliffs.
facts: It is sometimes called the 'Rose City' because of its pink stone.
Visitors reach it through a narrow canyon called the Siq.

landmarks.name: Burj Khalifa
landmarks.why: The tallest building in the world.
facts: It is about 828 metres tall.
Its shape was inspired by a desert flower.

landmarks.name: Mount Fuji
landmarks.why: Japan's tallest mountain, with an almost perfect cone shape.
facts: It is 3,776 metres tall.
Its snowy top can be seen from Tokyo on clear days.

landmarks.name: Mount Everest
landmarks.why: The highest mountain on Earth above sea level.
facts: It is 8,849 metres tall (measured in 2020).
In Nepal it is called Sagarmatha.

landmarks.name: Mount Kilimanjaro
landmarks.why: The highest mountain in Africa.
facts: It is about 5,895 metres tall.
It has snow near its top even though it is close to the Equator.

landmarks.name: Victoria Falls
landmarks.why: One of the largest waterfalls in the world.
facts: Its local name, Mosi-oa-Tunya, means 'the smoke that thunders'.
Its spray can be seen from many kilometres away.

landmarks.name: Parthenon
landmarks.why: A marble temple on the Acropolis, built for the goddess Athena.
facts: Its columns bulge slightly in the middle so they look straight from far away.
It sits on a rocky hill high above Athens.

landmarks.name: Chichén Itzá
landmarks.why: A great Maya city with a step pyramid called El Castillo.
facts: On the spring and autumn equinoxes, a shadow like a snake slides down the pyramid steps.
It is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

landmarks.name: Saint Basil's Cathedral
landmarks.why: Famous for its colourful onion-shaped domes.
facts: It stands in Red Square in Moscow.
It has nine chapels, each with its own dome.

landmarks.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
landmarks.why: A fairy-tale castle on a hill, built for King Ludwig II.
facts: It helped inspire famous fairy-tale castles in films.
It was never fully finished.

landmarks.name: Sagrada Família
landmarks.why: A giant church designed by Antoni Gaudí, famous for its shapes inspired by nature.
facts: Its building has gone on for more than 140 years.
Its columns look like tree trunks.

foods.name: Dosa
foods.fact: The batter is left overnight to ferment, which makes dosa light and crispy.

foods.name: Idli
foods.fact: Idlis are steamed, not fried — soft rice cakes often eaten with sambar and chutney.

foods.name: Biryani
foods.fact: Many cities have their own style, like Hyderabadi and Dindigul biryani.

foods.name: Sushi
foods.fact: The word sushi is about the sour vinegared rice, not the fish.

foods.name: Pizza
foods.fact: Pizza Margherita's colours — red, white and green — match Italy's flag.

foods.name: Pasta
foods.fact: Italy has hundreds of pasta shapes, like spaghetti, penne and farfalle (bow-ties).

foods.name: Tacos
foods.fact: A taco is eaten with your hands, folded around its filling.

foods.name: Croissant
foods.fact: Its many flaky layers come from folding butter into the dough again and again.

foods.name: Jiaozi (dumplings)
foods.fact: Families often make them together to eat at Chinese New Year.

foods.name: Paella
foods.fact: It comes from Valencia and is cooked in a wide, shallow pan.

foods.name: Pad Thai
foods.fact: It mixes sweet, sour and salty flavours in one dish.

foods.name: Kimchi
foods.fact: It is fermented, and Korean families often make big batches together in autumn.

foods.name: Feijoada
foods.fact: It is a slow-cooked bean stew often eaten on weekends.

foods.name: Injera
foods.fact: This spongy flatbread is used like a spoon to scoop up stews.

foods.name: Phở
foods.fact: It is a noodle soup often eaten for breakfast.

foods.name: Poutine
foods.fact: It comes from Quebec in Canada.

clothing.name: Sari
clothing.about: A long piece of cloth, often 5 to 9 metres, wrapped around the body and draped over the shoulder.

clothing.name: Veshti / Dhoti
clothing.about: A cloth wrapped around the waist, worn by men in Tamil Nadu (veshti) and across India (dhoti).

clothing.name: Kimono
clothing.about: A T-shaped robe with wide sleeves, tied with a sash called an obi.

clothing.name: Hanbok
clothing.about: Korean clothing with a short jacket and a full skirt or loose trousers, in bright colours.

clothing.name: Kilt
clothing.about: A knee-length wrapped skirt from Scotland, made in checked patterns called tartan.

clothing.name: Qipao (Cheongsam)
clothing.about: A fitted dress with a high collar, often made of silk.

clothing.name: Kente cloth
clothing.about: A colourful woven cloth from Ghana; each pattern and colour has a meaning.

clothing.name: Dirndl
clothing.about: A dress with a blouse, bodice and apron, traditional in Bavaria and the Alps.

clothing.name: Poncho
clothing.about: A warm blanket-like garment with a hole for the head, worn in the Andes.

festivals.name: Diwali
festivals.about: The festival of lights. Homes glow with oil lamps called diyas, and families share sweets.

festivals.name: Holi
festivals.about: The festival of colours, when people throw coloured powder and water to welcome spring.

festivals.name: Pongal
festivals.about: Tamil Nadu's harvest festival. Rice is boiled with milk and jaggery until it overflows — 'pongal'!

festivals.name: Chinese New Year
festivals.about: The start of the lunar new year, with red lanterns, dragon dances and family dinners.

festivals.name: Carnival
festivals.about: Brazil's giant party with samba dancing, music and colourful parades.

festivals.name: Christmas
festivals.about: Celebrated around the world with lights, carols, decorated trees and gifts.

festivals.name: Hanami
festivals.about: Picnics under blooming cherry trees to enjoy the pink blossoms.

festivals.name: Eid al-Fitr
festivals.about: Celebrated around the world at the end of Ramadan, with prayers, new clothes and sweet treats.

festivals.name: Día de Muertos
festivals.about: Families remember loved ones with marigold flowers, candles and colourful sugar skulls.

festivals.name: Songkran
festivals.about: Thai New Year, famous for friendly water fights in the streets.

festivals.name: Oktoberfest
festivals.about: A huge folk festival in Munich with music, rides and Bavarian food.

facts: Asia is the largest continent and has the most people.
It has the highest mountain, Mount Everest.
Asia.people: Asia has thousands of languages and many of the world's oldest cultures, from India and China to Japan and the Middle East.

facts: Africa has the longest river, the Nile.
The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world.
Africa.people: Africa has 54 countries and more than a thousand languages.

facts: Many European countries are small and close together.
The Alps are its most famous mountain range.
Europe.people: Europe has many languages, like French, German, Spanish and Italian, and is famous for castles and old cities.

facts: It stretches from the Arctic to the tropics.
Greenland, the world's largest island, is part of North America.
North America.people: Its biggest countries are Canada, the United States and Mexico; English, Spanish and French are widely spoken.

facts: The Amazon rainforest is the largest tropical rainforest on Earth.
The Andes are the longest mountain range above water.
South America.people: Most people speak Spanish or Portuguese; Brazil is the biggest country.

facts: Australia is both a country and the main land of this continent.
The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef system in the world.
Oceania.people: Oceania includes Australia, New Zealand and thousands of Pacific islands.

facts: Antarctica is the coldest, windiest and driest continent.
About 98% of it is covered by thick ice.
Antarctica.people: Nobody lives here all year — only scientists visit research stations.

in.climate: Hot and tropical in most places, with snowy mountains in the Himalayas and a rainy monsoon season.
facts: India has the largest population of any country.
Chess and the game of snakes and ladders first came from India.

cn.climate: From cold deserts in the north to warm, wet lands in the south.
facts: The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia.
Paper and printing were invented in China.

jp.climate: Four clear seasons, with snowy winters in the north and warm summers.
facts: Japan is made of more than 6,000 islands.
Its bullet trains are among the fastest in the world.

fr.climate: Mild and rainy in the north and west, sunny and dry by the Mediterranean.
facts: France is the most-visited country in the world.
It makes hundreds of different kinds of cheese.

it.climate: Warm, dry summers and mild winters, colder in the mountains.
facts: Italy is shaped like a boot.
Two tiny countries, Vatican City and San Marino, are inside Italy.

eg.climate: Very hot and dry desert, with almost no rain.
facts: Almost everyone in Egypt lives near the Nile.
Ancient Egyptians wrote with picture-symbols called hieroglyphs.

us.animal: Bald eagle (national bird); American bison (national mammal)
us.climate: Every kind — snowy Alaska, desert Arizona and tropical Hawaii.
facts: It has 50 states.
Yellowstone was the world's first national park.
Brazil is the largest country in South America.
People in Brazil speak Portuguese.

au.climate: Mostly dry, with tropical north and cooler south.
facts: Kangaroos and koalas live in the wild only in Australia (and nearby islands).
Australia is the only country that covers a whole continent's mainland.

gb.climate: Mild and often rainy all year.
facts: It is made up of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
London's Underground is the oldest underground railway in the world.

mx.climate: Hot deserts in the north, tropical forests in the south.
facts: Long ago, the Maya and Aztecs here made drinks from cacao, the bean chocolate comes from.
Mexico City was built on top of the old Aztec city Tenochtitlan.

ru.climate: Long, very cold winters and short summers.
facts: Russia is the largest country in the world.
Lake Baikal is the deepest lake in the world.

de.climate: Cool and rainy, with cold winters.
facts: Germany has more than 20,000 castles.
The printing press with movable type was made here by Gutenberg.

es.climate: Hot, sunny summers; cooler and wetter in the north.
facts: Spanish is one of the most-spoken languages in the world.
The Canary Islands are part of Spain.

ca.climate: Cold, snowy winters; warm summers in the south.
facts: Canada has the longest coastline of any country.
It has more lakes than the rest of the world combined.

za.climate: Mostly sunny and dry, with mild winters.
facts: South Africa has three capital cities.
It has 12 official languages.

ke.climate: Hot near the coast, cooler in the highlands.
facts: The Equator passes through Kenya.
Huge herds of wildebeest migrate through the Maasai Mara.

pe.climate: Dry coast, cold mountains and hot rainforest.
facts: Potatoes were first grown in the Andes of Peru.
Lake Titicaca, on its border, is one of the highest lakes people sail on.

np.climate: Warm in the south, icy cold in the high mountains.
facts: Eight of the world's ten highest mountains are in Nepal or on its borders.
Nepal's flag is the only national flag that is not a rectangle.

lk.climate: Tropical, warm and humid all year.
facts: Sri Lanka is an island south of India.
It is one of the world's biggest tea growers.

ae.climate: Very hot desert, with little rain.
facts: It is made up of seven emirates, including Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
The tallest building in the world, Burj Khalifa, is in Dubai.

gr.climate: Hot, dry summers and mild winters.
facts: The Olympic Games began in ancient Greece.
Greece has thousands of islands.

kr.climate: Four seasons, with hot summers and cold winters.
facts: Its alphabet, Hangul, was created in the 1400s.
Seoul is one of the most connected cities in the world.

th.climate: Tropical and hot, with a rainy season.
facts: Thailand was never colonised by a European country.
Its capital, Bangkok, is famous for floating markets.

ar.climate: Warm in the north, cold and windy in Patagonia in the south.
facts: Aconcagua is the highest mountain outside Asia.
The tango dance began in Argentina and Uruguay.

ng.climate: Hot all year, with a rainy season.
facts: Nigeria has more people than any other country in Africa.
More than 500 languages are spoken in Nigeria.
